literal: In old times Liu Yi at Jingkou brazenly asked for roast goose — how is this any different?
idiomatic: Long ago Liu Yi at Jingkou shamelessly demanded roast goose — is this not much the same?

literal: You are certainly a notable gentleman.
idiomatic: You are a true man of note.

literal: " Thereupon he ate with him at every meal.
idiomatic: " From then on he shared every meal with him.

literal: Juan's brother Zhongwen had learning and cultivation; under Wei he was Administrator of Gaoyang and Interior Minister of Qinghe.
idiomatic: Juan's brother Zhongwen pursued learning and held to what is right; under Wei he served as prefect of Gaoyang and interior minister of Qinghe.

literal: In the Xinghe era he was a staff member to the Chancellor.
idiomatic: In the Xinghe reign he was a staff officer to the chancellor.

literal: At the defeat at Shayuan, Zhongwen grasped a horse's tail to cross the river, now submerged, now emerging from the waves.
idiomatic: When Shayuan was lost, Zhongwen seized a horse's tail to ford the river, now swallowed by the water, now breaking the surface again.

literal: The Grand Ancestor saw him and said, "That is Staff Member Cui."
idiomatic: Gao Huan saw him and said, "That is Staff Officer Cui."

literal: He immediately sent a boat to fetch him.
idiomatic: At once he sent a boat to bring him in.

literal: Once across, he comforted him: "You acted for kin and for your lord, heedless of ten thousand deaths — one may call you a filial son at home and a loyal minister to the state."
idiomatic: When he had crossed, Gao Huan comforted him: "You risked everything for family and for your lord — at home a filial son, to the state a loyal minister."

literal: He was promoted to General of the Central Army.
idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the central army.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was made regular attendant-in-ordinary and grand master for splendid happiness.

literal: In the seventh year he died, aged sixty.
idiomatic: In the seventh year he died, aged sixty.

literal: His son Yan, during Wuping, served in succession as Palace Secretary and Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: His son Yan, in the Wuping era, served in turn as palace secretary and gentleman of the masters of writing.

literal: Yan's younger brother Biao had learning and knowledge with literary inventiveness; his bearing and tone were very lofty.
idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Biao was learned and quick of mind, with real literary gift; his manner and tone were very high.

literal: During Wuping he was Military Staff Officer in the Great Army Headquarters of the Prince of Langya.
idiomatic: In Wuping he was military staff officer in the great army headquarters of the Prince of Langya.

literal: He helped fix the Five Rites and awaited orders at the Wulin Hall.
idiomatic: He took part in fixing the Five Rites and awaited orders at the Forest of Letters Hall.

literal: Under Sui in Renshou he died while serving as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary with Unrestricted Access.
idiomatic: Under the Sui, in Renshou, he died in office as regular attendant-in-ordinary with unrestricted access.

literal: Shuren, under Wei Administrator of Ying Province.
idiomatic: Shuren served under Wei as administrator of Ying Province.

literal: His son Yanwu had discernment and capacity; Magistrate of Chaoge.
idiomatic: His son Yanwu had judgment and practical ability; he was magistrate of Chaoge.

literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang he was Governor of Wei Province.
idiomatic: At the opening of Sui Kaihuang he was governor of Wei Province.

literal: His son Kan, at the end of Wei also served as Unrestricted Regular Attendant and envoy on a mission to court Liang.
idiomatic: His son Kan, in the final years of Wei, also served as unrestricted regular attendant and went as envoy to the Liang court.

literal: His son Ji, at the beginning of Wuping was Master of the Palace Household; died while serving as Prefect of Wude Commandery.
idiomatic: His son Ji, at the start of Wuping, was master of the palace household; he died in office as prefect of Wude Commandery.

literal: His son Yu, Wei Administrator of Dongguan.
idiomatic: His son Yu was Wei administrator of Dongguan.

literal: His son Yue, Libationer to the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: His son Yue was libationer to the minister of works.

literal: Juan's clansman Jingfeng, styled Luanshu, was a great-great-grandson of Juan's fifth-generation ancestor Cheng's distant line.
idiomatic: Juan's clansman Jingfeng, styled Luanshu, was a great-great-grandson on the distant line of Juan's fifth-generation forebear Cheng.

literal: Jingfeng studied broadly and was famed for medical skill.
idiomatic: Jingfeng ranged through learning and won renown for medicine.

literal: Under Wei he was Imperial Physician-in-Chief of the Pharmacy; under Tianbao, Governor of Qiao Province.
idiomatic: Under Wei he was imperial physician-in-chief of the pharmacy; under Tianbao he was governor of Qiao Province.

literal: Jingfeng's elder brother Jingzhe, Wei Grand Master of Palace Counsel and Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Jingfeng's elder brother Jingzhe was, under Wei, grand master of palace counsel and chief clerk to the minister of works.

literal: His son Guo, styled Fajun, from youth loved learning, read widely in classics and histories, had many arts, and was especially skilled in physiognomy.
idiomatic: His son Guo, styled Fajun, loved learning from boyhood, read widely in the classics and histories, mastered many arts, and above all excelled at physiognomy.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was Imperial Physician-in-Chief of the Pharmacy; in Qianming he was appointed Administrator of Gaoyang Commandery and Master of the Heir Apparent's Household; in Wuping given Honorary Commissioner Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes; died while serving as Minister Herald.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was imperial physician-in-chief of the pharmacy; in Qianming he was made administrator of Gaoyang Commandery and master of the heir apparent's household; in Wuping he was given honorary commissioner equal in rank to the three dukes; he died in office as minister herald.

literal: Fajun was with the imperial procession at Jinyang in the sixth year of Wuping and once said to Secretariat Vice Director Li Delin: "Today in reading the physiognomy of civil and military officials from the Xiang prince and below, I saw each man's fate through to the end — I cannot bear to speak of it with my mouth."
idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wuping Fajun followed the imperial train at Jinyang and once told secretariat vice director Li Delin: "Today, reading the faces of civil and military men from the Prince of Xiang down, I saw each fate run to its end — my mouth cannot bear to say what I saw."

literal: Only my younger brother should know still greater wealth and honor; it will be in another state, not in our own court — I shall not live to see it either."
idiomatic: Only my younger brother will know still greater wealth and rank — in another realm, not in this court; I shall not live to see it either."

literal: His mastery was of this order.
idiomatic: Such was the fineness of his art.

literal: Juan's clansman Zhaoshi was grandson of Wei Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liang.
idiomatic: Juan's clansman Zhaoshi was grandson of Wei, vice director of the masters of writing Liang.

literal: His father Shitai was Remonstrating and Editing Grand Master.
idiomatic: His father Shitai was remonstrating and editing grand master.

literal: In youth Zhaoshi was careless and unrestrained; as he grew he changed his ways and became more careful and substantial.
idiomatic: In youth Zhaoshi was loose and unrestrained; as he matured he changed his ways and grew careful and solid.

literal: He ranged through classics and histories and had considerable literary thought.
idiomatic: He ranged through the classics and histories and had real literary turn of mind.

literal: He inherited his father's title, Baron of Leling.
idiomatic: He inherited his father's title, baron of Leling.

literal: Upon leaving the robe he was Sacrificial Wine of the Eastern Pavilion of the Opened Government, then transferred to Military Staff Officer in the Ministry of Works, promoted to Recording Master in the Great Army Headquarters.
idiomatic: Upon leaving the robe he was sacrificial wine of the eastern pavilion of the opened government, then transferred to military staff officer in the ministry of works, and promoted to recording master in the great army headquarters.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was transferred to Vice Director for Direct Access and was envoy to comfort Qing Province.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianping he was transferred to vice director for direct access and sent as envoy to comfort Qing Province.

literal: When he reached the border of Qi Province he was captured by local bandits such as Cui Kumarajiva and others.
idiomatic: When he reached the border of Qi Province, local bandits led by Cui Kumarajiva seized him.

literal: Zhaoshi held to integrity and did not waver; he explained fortune and misfortune to them, and the bandits thereupon released him.
idiomatic: Zhaoshi held to his integrity and did not stir; he set out fortune and ruin before them, and the bandits let him go.

literal: He then made a circuit to comfort the Qing circuit and returned.
idiomatic: He then made a circuit through the Qing region to offer comfort and returned.

literal: In the Yuanxiang era, several times as Palace Draftsman he received Liang envoys.
idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he several times, as palace draftsman, received Liang envoys.

literal: In the Wuding era he again concurrently served as Correcting Member and was sent as envoy with Liang envoys to Xuzhou.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he again concurrently served as correcting member and escorted Liang envoys to Xuzhou.

literal: On his return, he was ordered to compile the Imperial Diary.
idiomatic: On his return he was ordered to compile the imperial diary.

literal: Soon he also served as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary with Unrestricted Access and was deputy envoy on a mission to Liang.
idiomatic: Soon he also served as regular attendant-in-ordinary with unrestricted access and went as deputy envoy to Liang.

literal: Transferred to Secretariat Draftsman.
idiomatic: He was transferred to secretariat draftsman.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he helped fix the rites of abdication and elevation; enfeoffed Baron of Xiangcheng and still concurrently Secretariat Vice Director.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he took part in fixing the rites of abdication and enthronement; he was enfeoffed as baron of Xiangcheng and still held the post of secretariat vice director.

literal: In the second year he died, aged forty-nine at the time.
idiomatic: In the second year he died, aged forty-nine.

literal: The historian writes: Lan Gen early had reputation and conduct praised by contemporaries;
idiomatic: The historian writes: Lan Gen early won a name for conduct that men of the age praised;

literal: Changru's talent and standing were beautiful, valued by the age.
idiomatic: Changru's talent and bearing were splendid, and his own time held him in honor.

literal: Both shared in the achievements of hegemony, met with open, eminent preferment — with Li Yuanzhong and Lu Wenwei are they not figures of the righteous banner?
idiomatic: Both took part in the work of founding the realm and rose to open, shining rank — with Li Yuanzhong and Lu Wenwei, are they not men of the righteous banner?

literal: Wei attached himself to powerful favorites; the Cuis were arrogant by noble birth — though they had the beauty of the Duke of Zhou, it still counted as a stain on virtue; how much less could one use that to gauge their relative standing.
idiomatic: Wei courted the great and the favored; the Cuis leaned on birth and pride — though each bore something of the Duke of Zhou's grace, that still weighed on their moral credit, to say nothing of judging who stood higher or lower.

literal: Zhan's diction and rhythm were warm and elegant, his spirit bright and outgoing — a leader of his age as well.
idiomatic: Zhan's phrasing ran warm and fine, his spirit bright and quick to show — a leader among men of that day as well.

literal: The encomium says: Cui and Wei's talent and standing, valued at the dawn of hegemony.
idiomatic: The encomium says: Cui and Wei — talent and standing honored at the dawn of hegemony.

literal: The traces of moral teaching — were they not like a sickness?
idiomatic: The marks left on moral teaching — were they not its very sickness?

literal: Yantong cherished ambition; the family style had surplus.
idiomatic: Yantong held to high purpose; the family manner still had something to spare.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
